{"consolidated_memory":"**Recurring NaN Feature Issues in ml/features/encoder.py (Multiple Occasions)**

All incidents occurred in the ml pipeline, specifically in ml/features/encoder.py, with the common symptom of NaN values appearing in feature encoder output. The repro method for all three was encoding a batch holding the sparse column. However, each incident had distinct triggers, root causes, and fixes.

**Occasion 1: [2026-03-24]**
- Trigger: deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
- Root cause: serialiser dropping unknown fields
- Signal: NaN value in one output column
- Business result: 17 duplicate rows per day were being written; stopping the duplicates was the resolution
- Fix: switched to strict schema that rejects unknown fields
- PR #4004, branch fix/nan-feature-1
- Context: same corner of ml/features/encoder.py as earlier NaN feature work

**Occasion 2: [2026-08-07]**
- Trigger: manifested after client had already retried once
- Root cause: unbounded retry loop with no backoff strategy
- Signal: NaN value in one output column
- Business result: nightly rollup matched source counts for 76 days running after fix
- Fix: capped retry attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter
- PR #4828, branch fix/nan-feature-2
- Context: same corner of ml/features/encoder.py as earlier NaN feature work

**Occasion 3: [2026-08-12]**
- Trigger: only affected users sitting in negative UTC offset timezones
- Root cause: naive datetime being compared against an aware datetime object
- Signal: NaN value in one output column
- Business result: reclaimed 96 GB of blob storage after fix
- Fix: made every boundary timezone aware at the edge
- PR #7791, branch fix/nan-feature-3
- Context: same corner of ml/features/encoder.py as earlier NaN feature work"}
